title: Handling 4xx/5xx HTTP Statuses with HX-Retarget and HX-Reswap

progressiveExplaining.eli5: By default, if the server returns an error like '422 Invalid Password', HTMX thinks the request failed and refuses to update the page. With `HX-Retarget` and `HX-Reswap`, the server can say: 'Hey, this was an error, but take this error message and deliver it to `#error-box` instead of the main area.'
progressiveExplaining.junior: By default, HTMX **only swaps content on 2xx successful HTTP status codes**. If the server returns a 4xx (e.g. `400 Bad Request`, `422 Unprocessable Entity`) or 5xx error, HTMX triggers `htmx:responseError` and skips swapping. The server can override this behavior by returning the `HX-Retarget: #error-div` and `HX-Reswap: innerHTML` headers alongside the error status code to render validation errors.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, this reinforces REST semantics: rather than returning HTTP 200 for validation failures (a classic SPA anti-pattern), the server emits semantically correct HTTP status codes (`422 Unprocessable Entity` for form validation, `403 Forbidden` for auth). By utilizing response control headers (`HX-Retarget`, `HX-Reswap`, `HX-Trigger`), the backend dynamically changes the client swap destination based on the business outcome without client-side error parsing.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: In HTMX's response pipeline, `handleErrorFlag` checks `responseInfo.xhr.status`. If status is outside the 200-399 range, HTMX checks for `response-targets` extension or custom event overrides (`htmx:beforeOnLoad`). If the response contains `HX-Retarget`, HTMX updates `target = document.querySelector(headerValue)`. If `HX-Reswap` is present, it overrides the swap strategy and proceeds to swap the error payload.

codeComparison.title: Anti-Pattern HTTP 200 Fake Errors vs Semantic HTTP 422 + HX-Retarget
codeComparison.summary: Returning HTTP 200 for errors violates HTTP standards; HTTP 422 with `HX-Retarget` preserves semantics and redirects errors cleanly.

interviewGotchas.question: How can you configure HTMX to swap content on 4xx/5xx status codes globally without using server headers?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of HTMX global configuration and the `response-targets` extension.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: You can use the official **`response-targets` extension** (`hx-ext="response-targets"`) and declarative attributes like `hx-target-422="#validation-errors"` or `hx-target-500="#server-error"`. Alternatively, intercept `htmx:beforeOnLoad` in JS: `document.body.addEventListener('htmx:beforeOnLoad', (evt) => { if (evt.detail.xhr.status === 422) evt.detail.shouldSwap = true; });`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Without either `response-targets`, `HX-Retarget` headers, or `htmx:beforeOnLoad`, HTMX will completely ignore 4xx/5xx response bodies.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `HX-Retarget` and `HX-Reselect`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks precision regarding target location vs source fragment extraction.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `HX-Retarget: #some-id` changes the **destination element in the active DOM** where the response will be swapped. `HX-Reselect: #some-id` changes which **portion of the incoming HTML response** will be extracted and swapped into the target (equivalent to `hx-select`).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not confuse source selection (`HX-Reselect`) with destination target redirection (`HX-Retarget`).
